adopted: A reading-time floor per text element (0.8s for a label, 0.3s per word with a 1.2s minimum for a line), turned into a checker that emits review findings.
A nine-question plan rubric whose last question names the user flow (entry, key action, result) and biases the storyboard toward the product in use.
Beat policy: one to three strong-cue locks within 0.15s, small entrances within 0.10s, readable lines never on consecutive fast beats, locks marked in source.
Audio-reactive visuals as content not medium: no waveforms or bars; energy drives warmth, contrast and presence with small text scale swings.
Poster frame chosen at a settled beat and baked as frame 0 with an ffmpeg overlay so thumbnail grabbers show it.
A boundary statement naming which layer owns angle, copy and audio selection versus timing mechanics and render.
findings: The skill is prose and policy over an external renderer; its engine capabilities (check gate, beat detection, font aliasing) belong to that renderer, not to the skill.
Its own gain guidance produced a render near -27 LUFS; it has no loudness target, so a delivery loudness gate was needed.
Its inspect step reads landing-page HTML and CSS and does not capture a running product, which is the weaker path for anything beyond a static site.
Its bundled music is one artist's corporate library used for every video, in tension with its own specificity law.
Its tone presets are written for joke products and do not map to production brief workflows.
method: Installed the skill locally, ran it end to end on a real game repository with its renderer, audited where the wall-clock went, then read every reference file, the bundled asset analysis and the cue analyzer script before distilling the rules into a repository-owned skill with mechanical checks.
open_questions: Whether the scene text budget ratio (85 percent) should vary by workflow.
Whether a portrait reframe needs its own floor constants once real portrait cuts are measured.
question: Which rules in the /brag launch-video skill make its output good, and how should they be carried into Video Studio without its renderer coupling?
rejected: Copying the bundled music, sound effects or their analysis files.
Depending on a specific renderer's skills or CLI inside the rules.
Reading a landing page as the source of truth when the product can be captured running.
skipped: The optional narration path (single-provider local TTS) because narration is owned by Video Studio's own voice tooling.
The cue analyzer script because a beat detector already exists in the renderer path and the policy only needs a beat grid.

findings: Defines the creative laws, reading-time floor, plan rubric, beat policy, audio policy and poster technique that were reimplemented.
MIT licensed prose; no files were copied into the derived skill.
